group: MurmurHash3.hash32(long, int) – deterministic behavior and seed sensitivity

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., result1). Re‑invoking hash32(0L, 104729) must return the same result.
cases.description: Verify that the method returns a consistent hash for the zero long value with the default seed.

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., result2) that is different from the result of case 1.
cases.description: Check handling of the maximum long value with a zero seed; result must be repeatable and distinct from the zero‑data case.

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., result3) that differs from results of cases 1 and 2.
cases.description: Validate that a negative long value and a negative seed are processed correctly and produce a unique hash.
Typical non‑trivial data value with a positive seed; ensures the byte‑reversal and two‑mix steps are exercised.

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., result5) that is NOT equal to result4.
cases.description: Same data as previous case but with a different seed; verifies that the seed influences the final hash.
All‑bits‑set long value with zero seed, exercising the full 64‑bit reversal and both mix calls.

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., result7) that differs from case 1 (different seed).
cases.description: Zero data with zero seed, confirming that changing only the seed changes the hash.

group: MurmurHash3.hash32(long, int) – additional boundary and seed variations

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., resultA) that is reproducible on repeated calls and differs from hashes of other data/seed combos.
cases.description: Small positive long with the maximum positive seed tests handling of low‑order bits and extreme seed value.

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., resultB) distinct from the hash of (-1L, 0) already covered.
cases.description: All‑bits‑set long with the most negative seed verifies correct sign‑extension and mixing for extreme seed values.

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., resultC) that differs from hashes of data where high and low 32‑bit halves are swapped.
cases.description: Data where only the low 32 bits are set ensures the first mix step processes non‑zero low part while the second mix processes zero high part.

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., resultD) distinct from resultC, confirming that high‑half‑only data is handled correctly.
cases.description: Data where only the high 32 bits are set tests the second mix step with a non‑zero value while the first mix receives zero.

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., resultE) that is different from the hash of Long.MAX_VALUE with seed 0 (existing case).
cases.description: Maximum positive long with a negative seed checks proper handling of signed seeds and ensures seed influences the final hash.

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., resultF) that differs from the hash of Long.MIN_VALUE with seed -1 (existing case).
cases.description: Minimum long value (only the sign bit set) with zero seed validates correct byte‑reversal and mixing for this edge pattern.

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., resultG) distinct from hashes of other patterned data.
cases.description: Sequential byte pattern tests that the byte‑reversal step correctly reorders bytes before mixing.

cases.expected: A deterministic 32‑bit int value (e.g., resultH) that is not equal to resultG, confirming that different byte orders produce different hashes.
cases.description: Reverse sequential byte pattern ensures that the reversal logic is not a no‑op and influences the hash.
